prompts_findings.prompt_lead: I'm in a training where I'll build a working memory around one live challenge I'

risks_fired.evidence: "Ask me these in turn" is too soft per check_prompts.md rule 15 on its own, but the body prose immediately after the fence names the failure mode and gives the recovery move: "If it shows all three questions at once, push back and ask for one at a time." Body-callout carve-out (prompt-behavior.md's question-dump carve-out) applies — downgraded to low.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Carve-out already satisfies the rule; no change required. Optional strengthening: structural enforcement inside the fence ("Ask one question at a time; wait for my answer before the next; don't show me the full list") would remove reliance on student-initiated push-back.

risks_fired.evidence: Conversational framing ("Help me pin the challenge down") invites a brief acknowledgment before Q1 lands; only 3 named sub-steps, below the 4+ structural trigger in check_prompts.md rule 17.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Low risk, acceptable as-is; no suppressor needed at this length.

risks_fired.evidence: "write a one-paragraph brief to ./challenge.md" carries no instruction to preserve the student's specific, possibly-uncomfortable phrasing (e.g. "I don't know if my team even wants this"); default regeneration tone can drift toward generic-competent summary language.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Optional: add "keep the brief in my own words — the specific stakes and stuck point, not a smoothed-over summary" to the fence.

prompts_findings.prompt_lead: Based on the challenge brief you just wrote, suggest where I'd go looking for ra

risks_fired.evidence: Prompt asks for "2 to 3 practitioners (named people — writers, operators, researchers) worth reading on this challenge" with no link or source request, so the format-correct-but-unverified cargo-cult shape doesn't fully apply. Residual risk: named practitioners may be generic or poorly matched to the student's specific challenge rather than genuinely relevant to it.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Optional body callout after the fence: "Claude's practitioner picks can run generic — treat as a starting list, not a curated one." Or anchor inside the fence: "avoid generic names that would fit any challenge in this space."

risks_fired.evidence: "Keep it short" can be satisfied with broadly-recognisable, safe suggestions (well-known adjacent-domain names, generic Confluence search terms) rather than suggestions genuinely tailored to the student's specific challenge.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Low risk; the existing body follow-up ("Scan the list... circle the two or three you'd actually go pull first") already builds in a student-side quality check.
